problems.statement: Group-wide kitchen inefficiency (19 min vs 12 benchmark) is not a real problem: the ~17.6 min ticket time has been stable since the deliberate Oct 2024 Made Here redesign, which the board knowingly accepted, and the 12-min benchmark is not comparable (panel limited to chains with 60%+ pre-prepared/frozen components, scratch kitchens excluded).
The 19.1 min group average is inflated by Riverside alone; the other eight locations are at 17.6 and unchanged, so the headline figure misrepresents the group.

Riverside's slowdown since August 2026 is a localized staffing/capacity failure: loss of its saute/pasta line cook (Delgado) with no replacement or transfer, leaving the station run by a cross-training prep cook on Fri/Sat and the sous chef on weekday lunches.

Riverside's staffing gap is sustained by group operations/new ownership deferring transfer requests pending a staffing review, plus the group labor standard and a post-bridge-closure Sunday hours cut; this is a systemic/ownership-process cause more than a GM personal failing.
Riverside GM Tom Kessler's Sunday hours cut caused Delgado's resignation, making the GM the root cause needing replacement.

Moving to par-cooked/frozen components will fix speed and improve the business; it risks the food-quality differentiator that supports the premium check, satisfaction and sales growth, and would not address Riverside's station staffing problem.
Slow ticket times are hurting group guest satisfaction and repeat business.
Tying GM bonuses to a 12-minute ticket time would produce metric gaming (KDS bumping) or quality damage rather than real speed improvement.
The Oct 2024 menu redesign drove the rise in repeat visits.

causalClaims.to: group ticket time rise from ~13.5 to ~17.6 min

causalClaims.from: Riverside saute/pasta cook departure and unfilled position
causalClaims.to: Riverside ticket time rise to ~31 min, falling reviews and higher comps

causalClaims.from: group operations deferral of transfer requests

causalClaims.to: Riverside guest dissatisfaction and rating decline
gamed (bumped) tickets rather than faster service
inference that the rest of the group will follow

actions.action: Immediately fill Riverside's saute/pasta capacity: approve a transfer or temporary cook from another location and expedite the open requisition; end the deferral pending staffing review for Riverside.
actions.rationale: The Riverside degradation is traced to a specific unfilled station, and the fix is within ownership's control.

actions.action: Accelerate cross-training and station support for Jamal Ortiz and align Riverside's line scheduling with forecast covers, restoring Fri/Sat dinner staffing to 4 line positions.
actions.rationale: Time is concentrated on the saute/pasta station on busy nights, so restoring full station coverage targets the cause directly.

actions.action: Do not standardize all nine kitchens on par-cooked/frozen components.
actions.rationale: Eight kitchens are stable, the slower scratch menu was a deliberate choice behind higher check, food-quality scores and above-segment sales, and the 2024 trial showed quality damage.

actions.action: Do not write a 12-minute ticket-time target into GM bonuses.
actions.rationale: The target is based on a non-comparable benchmark and a prior ticket-time bonus led to KDS bumping with no guest benefit.

actions.action: Do not replace Riverside's GM on the current evidence.
actions.rationale: The slowdown tracks the vacancy and ownership's deferred transfers, and the claim that the GM caused the resignation is unproven and contradicted by other accounts.

actions.action: Re-benchmark against scratch-cooking or made-to-order peers and replace the 12-minute benchmark with a group-specific standard, treating 19 minutes as the board-set ceiling.
actions.rationale: The current benchmark excludes scratch kitchens, so a comparable one is needed before any ticket-time target.

actions.action: Hold a neutral exit-reason review for Delgado and a review of Riverside's staffing and labor-standard rules after the bridge closure.
actions.rationale: Competing accounts of why he left need resolving before any judgment on Riverside management.

actions.action: If speed is a goal, run targeted station-level improvements at the slowest stations in the stable eight rather than changing the menu.
actions.rationale: This could trim time without sacrificing the quality positioning, but the guest data show little demand for it.

nextEvidence: Neutral account of why Delgado resigned (contact for a completed exit interview, any written notice) and whether other Riverside cooks are at risk of leaving
Benchmark ticket times and satisfaction for scratch/made-to-order casual-dining peers with comparable average checks
Recovery trend at Riverside after a cook is added or transferred (KDS saute/pasta times, covers, reviews) to confirm the causal link
output.summary: The group is not inefficient. Eight kitchens run a steady 17.6 minutes, set by the board's deliberate 2024 scratch-menu redesign, and they earn higher satisfaction, check size and sales growth. The 12-minute benchmark covers only chains using frozen or pre-prepared components. Riverside alone is broken: after its saute/pasta cook left in August, the position stayed unfilled, and ownership deferred two transfer requests. That vacancy accounts for the group average's rise to 19.1. Fill Riverside's station now. Don't go frozen, don't tie bonuses to ticket time (a 2023 incentive led to bumped tickets), and don't replace the GM on this evidence.
